Set: Ancient Rome

Cicero
Marcus Tullius Cicero (106-43 BCE) was one of the most prominent Roman statesmen and orators of the first century BCE. He is considered the greatest Roman orator, and his works on law, politics, philosophy, and rhetoric are some of the most important surviving texts from ancient Rome. Cicero is also known for his role in defending the rights of Roman citizens and opposing tyranny.

Sallust
Gaius Sallustius Crispus (86-35 BCE) was a Roman historian, politician, and writer. He is best known for his two surviving works: "The Conspiracy of Catiline" and "The Jugurthine War." These works provide insight into political and military events of his time, and they are written in a vivid and dramatic style that has made them popular with readers throughout history.

Cleopatra
Cleopatra VII Philopator (69-30 BCE) was the last active ruler of the Ptolemaic Kingdom of Egypt. She was a master of diplomacy and a patron of the arts, as well as a powerful and charismatic leader. Cleopatra is famous for her relationships with Julius Caesar and Mark Antony, and she is often depicted in art and literature as a beautiful and seductive figure.

Augustus
Gaius Octavius (63 BCE-14 CE), better known as Augustus, was the founder of the Roman Empire and its first emperor. He is considered one of the most successful politicians in history, and his reign marked the transition from the Roman Republic to the Roman Empire. Augustus is known for his reforms, his expansion of the empire, and his efforts to restore order and stability after years of civil war.
